channel.title: Weekly Research Digest
channel.description: New papers in economic theory, innovation, IO and AI from leading journals.

item.title: Rethinking Distribution Shifts: Empirical Analysis and Modeling for Tabular Data
item.description: Different distribution shifts require different interventions, and algorithms must be grounded in the specific shifts they address. — Tianyu Wang, Jiashuo Liu, Peng Cui, Hongseok Namkoong

item.title: Redeploying the Jockeys: The Intermediary Role of Venture Capital in Entrepreneurial Labor Markets
item.description: This paper explores how venture capitalists (VCs) add value by examining their role as labor market intermediaries. Using novel data, I show that VCs create internal labor markets (ILMs) to facilitate entrepreneurial mobility across their portfolio firms. — Zhongchen Hu

item.title: Human Performance at Solving 0-1 Knapsack Problems: Results from a Large-Scale Field Experiment
item.description: The 0-1 knapsack problem is a fundamental problem of discrete choice that permeates many diverse fields and applications, but relatively little is known about what instances human solvers find more difficult than others. — Sumit Agarwal, Joel Goh, Wenlan Qian, Xin Zou

item.title: The Data-Driven Censored Newsvendor Problem
item.description: We study a censored variant of the data-driven newsvendor problem, where the decision maker must select an ordering quantity that minimizes expected overage and underage costs based only on offline censored sales data rather than historical demand realizations. — Chamsi Hssaine, Sean R. Sinclair

item.title: Banking on a Corporate Rebrand
item.description: Firms often rebrand to counter negative shocks, but can it work? — Matthew Jaremski, Kris James Mitchener, Kilian Rieder

item.title: Recommender Systems Under Privacy Protection
item.description: We examine how a profit-driven platform designs its recommender policies under varying privacy protection regimes. We demonstrate a functional equivalence between opt-out protection and unprotected privacy. — Can Küçükgül, Özalp Özer, Shouqiang Wang

item.title: Uncertainty Attitudes, Subjective Beliefs, and Decisions Under Uncertainty
item.description: We conducted survey experiments to gather new data on uncertainty attitudes and subjective beliefs. Our survey targets a general population, focusing on health and financial decisions. — Adeline Delavande, Jayant Ganguli, Friederike Mengel

item.title: Incumbents’ Alliances and (Non-)Adaptation During the Pre-Commercialization Stage of a New Technology
item.description: Research on incumbent adaptation through alliances typically assumes that incumbents can entice partners to share proprietary knowledge in a new technology by offering access to valuable complementary assets. — Jung-Hyun Suh, J.P. Eggers

item.title: Interface as a design choice: How the implementation of interfaces influences coordination and performance in modular systems
item.description: Research Summary Modular systems play a central role in technological innovation. Such systems emerge when interdependencies among modules in a complex system are isolated through interfaces. — Daniel Albert, Martin Ganco

item.title: Growth Paths in Early Machine Learning Ventures: Technical Configuration and Competitive Advantage Over Time
item.description: Machine learning capabilities have become important strategic assets, yet little is known about how their technical characteristics affect the competitive advantage of the firms that build them. — Jack Fraser, Pinar Ozcan

item.title: Knowledge protection and modularity of innovation activities in firms: Evidence from US trade secrecy law
item.description: Research Summary Strategy scholars have theoretically explored the relationship between legal knowledge protection and modularity of innovation activities in firms, but this relationship has yet to be empirically tested in the literature. — Eunkwang Seo, Christopher P. Dinkel

item.title: The Impact of Commercial Real Estate Regulations on U.S. Output
item.description: Commercial real estate accounts for about 20% of the U.S. capital stock and is highly regulated. Yet relatively little is known about how these regulations affect economic activity or consumer welfare. — Fil Babalievsky, Kyle F Herkenhoff, Lee E Ohanian, Edward C Prescott

item.title: Deregulation, Market Structure, and the Evolution of U.S. Banking
item.description: We construct novel network-based measures of U.S. state-level bank deregulation intensity that allow us to separately identify the effects of deregulation on competition and investment opportunities. — Emilio Bisetti, Stephen A. Karolyi, Stefan Lewellen

item.title: A platform for change? Core component innovations, complementor adaptation, and multihoming in platform‐based ecosystems
item.description: Research Summary Digital platforms coordinate complementor innovations through interfaces into their core components. — Shiva Agarwal, Ram Ranganathan

item.title: When money isn't everything: Identifying stage‐based patterns of entrepreneurial resource acquisition
item.description: Research Summary Scholars often examine how entrepreneurs' existing ties predict resource acquisition. We investigated the reverse: How does the act of pitching generate new ties with investors? — Esther Leibel, Denise Falchetti, Siobhan O'Mahony

item.title: Signaling in Repeated Delegation
item.description: — Parimal Bag, Wing Suen

item.title: Deadly Disease, Fear, and Ostracism in the Credit Market
item.description: This paper exploits the 2014 U.S. Ebola outbreak as a natural experiment to examine how fear distorts mortgage credit allocation. — Sumit Agarwal, Pengsheng Lin, Yupeng Lin, Ruichang Lu, Xiaojun Zhang

item.title: Whiplash: Congestion Dissipation in a Disrupted Circulatory Shipping System
item.description: The (post)pandemic period was marked by numerous port disruptions, leading to delays and rising costs for shippers. — Ming Hu, Chaoyu Zhang

item.title: Advertising by Recruiting Influencers
item.description: The rise of social media platforms has enabled customers to rely on influencers and peer reviews to guide their purchasing decisions. As products increasingly focus on experiences, firms are leveraging influencer marketing as a crucial tool. — Maya Jalloul, Vasiliki Kostami

item.title: Opinion Trumps Fact: Entry and Competition in Online Political News
item.description: This paper examines how new entrants influenced content strategies in the U.S. online political news business from 2014 to 2021. — Aaron Chatterji, Sharique Hasan, William D. Miles, Dror Shvadron

item.title: Drifting to the top? The effects of category erraticism on status mobility in the U.S. venture capital industry
item.description: Research Summary We examine the effects of category erraticism, that is, having moved across socio‐cognitively distant industry categories over time, on status mobility. — Danyang Li, Michael Jensen

item.title: Accommodation in the vertical supply chain: Implications of manufacturer dual tracking
item.description: Research Summary The prevalence of dual tracking, in which upstream manufacturers simultaneously produce branded and private‐label products for downstream retailers, has increased substantially in recent years, driven by growing consumer demand for private‐label products. — Young Hou

item.title: Do Fund Managers’ Commitments to Responsible Investing Affect Private Information Acquisition, Information Environment, and Corporate Sustainability?
item.description: We investigate the effects of mutual funds’ commitments to responsible investing on their information acquisition activities and the corresponding externalities for other stakeholders. — Sumit Agarwal, Johan Sulaeman, Yue Zhang, Zhe Zong

item.title: Wrongdoers or Saviors? CEO Activism, Media Partisanship, and the Media’s Construction of CEO Infamy and Celebrity
item.description: This study advances research on social evaluations by theorizing how partisan media construct CEO infamy through dramaturgical logics distinct from those underlying CEO celebrity. — G. Alessandra Alessandra Rizzi, Vilmos F. Misangyi

item.title: Strategic search: Adaptation of internal fit and market positioning under competition
item.description: Research Summary Firms seeking competitive advantage need both internal fit and a distinctive market position, yet strategy research says little about how the search for the two is related. — Gianluigi Giustiziero, Aseem Kaul, Dirk Martignoni

item.title: Investors' ideology and corporate symbolic and substantive climate actions
item.description: Research Summary Prior research suggests that institutional investors' liberalism is associated with firms' engagement in environmental sustainability, yet whether this association manifests in symbolic or substantive actions remains unclear. — Chang Liu, Wei Shi

item.title: Two-Sided Search in International Markets
item.description: — Jonathan Eaton, David Jinkins, James Tybout, Daniel Yi Xu

item.title: Connectors and Influencers
item.description: We study a setting in which personal acquisition of information is costly and maintaining personal contacts to share information socially is also costly. — Frédéric Moisan, Syngjoo Choi, Sanjeev Goyal

item.title: The Asymmetry in Responsible Investing Preferences and Beliefs
item.description: Empirical stylized facts in the literature concerning “sin” versus “angel” stocks display marked asymmetries in investor behavior. — Jacquelyn Humphrey, Shimon Kogan, Jacob S. Sagi, Laura T. Starks

item.title: Comparing Factor Models Under Regime Switching
item.description: We compare factor pricing models using the “test-asset irrelevance” result but under regime switching. We show that the unconditional squared Sharpe ratio measure is no longer appropriate for model comparison when returns are subject to regime shifts. — Shamim Ahmed, Cesare Robotti, Daniel Tsvetanov, Xiaoxia Ye

item.title: Effortful vs. Opportunistic Consumption of Discretionary Time: How Time-Reporting Decisions Influence Extra-Role Effort
item.description: Employees often work under incomplete contracts, performing both contracted in-role tasks and valuable but noncontracted extra-role activities. — Sophie Maussen

item.title: Can Voluntary Corporate Transparency Curb Corruption? Community-Level Evidence from Oil and Gas Fields in Africa
item.description: Voluntary corporate transparency seeks to promote accountability through disclosure, but substantive reporting does not by itself guarantee societal benefits. — Shirley Tang, Daniel W Elfenbein, Tatenda M Pasipanodya

item.title: Does innovation success need advocacy? Stakeholder involvement in firm innovation
item.description: Research Summary Prior research documents that firms often collaborate with advocacy groups to mitigate stakeholder contention. — Paolo Carioli, Christoph Grimpe, Karin Hoisl, Wolfgang Sofka

item.title: Platform development in incumbent firms: The interplay of data and actor interests in adding platforms to existing businesses
item.description: Research Summary Despite growing interest in platform transitions, limited research examines how firms navigate challenges of building platform businesses alongside existing products. — Jack Fraser, Elizabeth J. Altman, Pinar Ozcan

item.title: Designing for unanticipated uses: How product attributes shape community‐led exaptation
item.description: Research Summary Users often discover new uses for products that firms may later commercialize, which we call community‐led exaptation. We examine how product attributes shape users' discovery of new functions versus new functionalities. — Shi‐Ying Lim, Tian Heong Chan

item.title: Are client ties pre‐entry resources? Performance implications of client tie diversification
item.description: Research Summary This study investigates client tie diversification, where firms enter markets with existing clients. — Heejung Byun

item.title: The Welfare Effects of Price Shocks and Household Relief Packages: Evidence from an Energy Crisis
item.description: Aggregate price shocks generate unequal welfare losses both across and within income groups.Policymakers face a trade-off: price subsidies direct more support to households facing larger losses, but create inefficiencies, while transfers are less… — Peter Levell, Martin O'Connell, Kate Smith

item.title: Geographic Integration and Firm Exports: Evidence from China,
item.category: Journal of the European Economic Association
item.description: Domestic connectivity via passenger transport infrastructure can affect a country’s exports by easing information frictions. — Lin Tian, Yue Yu

item.title: What’s at Stake? Understanding the Role of Home Equity in Flood Insurance Demand
item.description: Changing flood insurance demand shifts climate risk across homeowners, lenders, and governments. We show that flood insurance take-up follows rising and falling home equity over the housing boom and bust across markets with different price dynamics. — Yanjun (Penny) Liao, Philip Mulder

item.title: Biodiversity Risk in the Corporate Bond Market
item.description: We show that a biodiversity risk premium has emerged in the U.S. corporate bond market following the United Nations Biodiversity Conference (COP15) in October 2021. — Sevgi Soylemezgil, Cihan Uzmanoglu

item.title: The Economics of Waste Valorization
item.description: As the spread of waste imposes substantial environmental and economic burdens, a newer operational strategy, waste valorization, is gaining attention. — Yuefeng Li, Zhongbin Wang, Shenghai Zhou

item.title: Firm divisionalization and the gender gap in CEO promotion
item.description: Research Summary This study examines how divisionalized firm structures shape the gender gap in internal chief executive officer (CEO) promotion. — Tingyu Du, Ulya Tsolmon

item.title: Strategy as a theory of change
item.description: Research Summary The theory‐based view argues that a strategist's task is to develop a theory to move the organization to an improved future state. — Sergio G. Lazzarini, Todd R. Zenger, Teppo Felin

item.title: Beliefs and the Incentive Effects of Preferential College Admissions: Evidence from an Experiment and a Structural Model
item.description: — Michela Maria Tincani, Fabian Kosse, Enrico Miglino

item.title: Noisy Global Value Chains
item.description: — Ha Bui, Zhen Huo, Andrei Levchenko, Nitya Pandalai-Nayar

item.title: Labor Market Tightness and the Reversal of Inequality Trends in Germany
item.description: Germany experienced a sharp rise in wage inequality over the two decades leading up to the Great Recession. — Christian Dustmann, Martin Friedrich, Carl Gergs, Uta Schönberg

item.title: Aspiring to a Better Future: Can a Simple Psychological Intervention Reduce Poverty?
item.description: Do higher aspirations for the future motivate people living in poverty to make long-term investments? Do their aspirations increase when economic conditions improve? — Kate Orkin, Robert Garlick, Mahreen Mahmud, Richard Sedlmayr, Johannes Haushofer, Stefan Dercon

item.title: Daddy’s Girl: Daughters, Managerial Decisions, and Gender Inequality
item.description: Using Danish registry data, we study how managers’ gender attitudes shape gender inequality in the workplace by exploiting the birth of a daughter—as opposed to a son—as a plausibly exogenous shock to male managers’ gender attitudes. — Maddalena Ronchi, Nina Smith

item.title: Learning‐by‐twinning: Organizational digital twins and the future of search
item.description: Research Summary Entrepreneurs and managers often need to evaluate strategic choices, such as redesigning an incentive plan or entering an unfamiliar market, before committing scarce resources. — Prithwiraj (Raj) Choudhury, Yingxin Du, Megan Lawrence

item.title: Generative AI use in entrepreneurship: An integrative review and the Empowerment–Entrapment Framework
item.description: Research Summary Despite the growing use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in entrepreneurship, research on its impact remains fragmented. — Jackson G. Lu, Gerui Gloria Zhao, Anna Manyi Zheng

item.title: Generative AI and the ability of entrepreneurial opportunities to generate sustained competitive advantages
item.description: Research Summary This paper examines how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) affects the ability of entrepreneurial opportunities to generate sustained competitive advantage. — Haiyang Zhang, Robert Wuebker, Jay B. Barney

item.title: When machines learn with organizations: AI‐enabled knowledge creation and entrepreneurship
item.description: Research Summary To promote entrepreneurship and new business development, firms will increasingly rely on new forms of knowledge creation to manage environments marked by technological change and radical uncertainty. — Linhui Wu, Shaker A. Zahra, Niron Hashai

item.title: Artificial intelligence and venture capital: Revisiting sourcing, selection, and nurturing activities
item.description: Research Summary Venture capital (VC) is an information‐intensive form of entrepreneurial finance conducted under extreme uncertainty. — Gary Dushnitsky

item.title: Entrepreneurship and Financial Deregulation
item.description: We quantitatively analyze the impact of US banking deregulation in the 1980s on the aggregate economy. Using recent econometric techniques, we first reexamine existing empirical evidence on the real effects of banking deregulation. — Toshihiko Mukoyama, Gang Zhang

item.title: Entrepreneurial theorizing with generative artificial intelligence
item.description: Research Summary Whether large language model (LLM) assistance changes how entrepreneurs construct theories remains unclear. — Sung Ho Park, Alex Murray

item.title: The intelligence loop and value creation in the age of AI agents
item.description: Research Summary Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving from generating outputs to executing work. An agent that executes work autonomously produces something generative AI does not: operational experience that can raise its future intelligence. — Yong Li, Ming Zeng, Alexis Li

item.title: “Borrowing intelligence to build a business”: The promise of open‐source AI for entrepreneurship
item.description: Research Summary Open‐source artificial intelligence (OSAI) is an increasingly important yet poorly understood frontier for entrepreneurial activity. — Georg von Krogh, Ann‐Kristin Weiser, Patrick Nicolas Tinguely

item.title: New wine, old bottles? Effective strategies of new GenAI firms
item.description: Research Summary Blending insights from GenAI, strategic reasoning, and empirical grounding in five illustrative ventures, we contribute a theoretical framework for effective strategies of new GenAI firms. — Kathleen M. Eisenhardt, Xilan Zhang

item.title: Generative AI and the architecture of knowledge work: Expertise bypass, exchange governability, and shifting bottlenecks
item.description: Research Summary Research on GenAI and work has largely focused on tasks. We ask when task‐level effects alter knowledge‐work industry architecture: the allocation of activities across firm boundaries. — Michael G. Jacobides, Mingyu Dalbert Ma, Amartya Das, Matt Langione, Sesh Iyer

item.title: Conceptual search: A generative view of entrepreneurial imagination
item.description: Research Summary Entrepreneurs cannot pursue ventures they never imagine. This article develops a generative view of entrepreneurial imagination as the construction of an evolving candidate set through generation, provisional evaluation, and revision. — Felipe A. Csaszar

item.title: Value creation and capture in artificial intelligence‐enabled ecosystems
item.description: Research Summary We develop an ecosystem perspective on AI‐enabled value creation, grounded in AI's characteristics as a general‐purpose technology. — Rahul Kapoor, Manav Raj

item.title: Labor Market Monopsony Power and the Dynamic Gains to Openness Reforms
item.description: We embed labor market monopsony into a dynamic heterogeneous‐firm general equilibrium model with exporting, horizontal FDI, and rich firm lifecycle dynamics. — Priyaranjan Jha, Antonio Rodriguez‐Lopez, Adam Hal Spencer

item.title: Entry and Welfare in General Equilibrium With Heterogeneous Firms and Endogenous Markups
item.description: We analyze market entry efficiency in single‐ and two‐sector closed‐economy Melitz–Ottaviano (MO) models without an outside good. Comparing market and second‐best outcomes, we find that market entry is efficient in the single‐sector model. — Kyle Bagwell, Seung Hoon Lee

item.title: Everything everywhere all‐at‐once? AI, expertise–output decoupling, and new entrepreneurial strategy trade‐offs in the age of abundance
item.description: Research Summary Generative AI democratizes entrepreneurship by lowering barriers to ideation, creating an environment of abundance. Yet while AI produces speed, scale, and local autonomy, these benefits may come at hidden costs to output quality. — Jen Gennai, Riitta Katila, Minu Kumar, Ian Sinapuelas

item.title: Public support and VC financing in academic startups
item.description: Research Summary We investigate public support and venture capital (VC) investment in academic startups. Government support may enable follow‐on investment by providing a quality signal to investors. — Maud Thys, Maikel Pellens, Hanna Hottenrott, Marius Berger

item.title: Startup multihoming in enterprise software ecosystems: The role of skill breadth and organizational learning
item.description: Research Summary We investigate startup decisions to multihome to another platform. — Vijayaraghavan Venkataraman, Marco Ceccagnoli, Chris Forman

item.title: The cost of the buzz? A sufficiency threshold perspective on digital transformation disclosure and cost of equity capital
item.description: Firms disclose information about complex internal activities to keep capital markets informed about their long-term value. — Lane Matthews, Julian M. Müller, Nikolai Kazantsev, Mariano L.M. Heyden

item.title: Learning from success but not from failure in digital experimentation
item.description: — Berk Deniz, Quang Nguyen, Pedro Sequeira

item.title: Government‐funded experimentation: How startups use R&D contracts to resolve uncertainty
item.description: Research Summary Startups use experimentation to reduce technological and market uncertainty, but experimentation is costly and unevenly funded. — Larisa Cioaca

item.title: It's a match! Similarity in personality traits in the business angel–founder dyad and follow‐on funding
item.description: Research summary We assess how personality alignment in investor–founder dyads is associated with the likelihood of follow‐on funding, a vital outcome for early‐stage ventures. — Angela Altmeier, Christian Fisch

item.title: Whither business model innovation strategy in the age of AI?
item.description: Research Summary We argue that business models are transformed into auto‐adaptive systems through embedded AI inference and learning activities. — Christoph Zott, Raphael Amit

item.title: Theorizing future phenomena: Metaverse, wearables, and humanoids
item.description: Research Summary We propose that entrepreneurship and strategy research can develop theory about phenomena of the future rather than only explain those of the past. — Andy Wu, Ronald Wang

item.title: Strong Nash equilibria of core-selecting double auctions
item.description: We study core-selecting auctions for double auctions that incorporate package bidding. — Shuntaro Kawachi

item.title: Framing the unknowable: The role of language and frame multiplicity in early‐stage startup pitches
item.description: Research Summary Early‐stage startup pitches must make largely unknowable futures plausible. As such, they bear a rhetorical burden. This study theorizes how multiple frames jointly shape this burden and, consequently, affect investor evaluations. — Ann‐Sophie Kowalewski

item.title: Re‐thinking academic entrepreneurship: Micro, meso, and macro perspectives
item.description: Research Summary We summarize and synthesize the papers contained in the special issue and use these studies to illustrate key micro, meso, and macro dimensions of academic entrepreneurship, where micro focuses on the scientist, meso is concerned with the… — Maribel Guerrero, Donald Siegel, Mirjam Knockaert, Phillip Phan, Miriam Erez

item.title: Unveiling the J-curve: How intangibles drive productivity mismeasurement
item.description: — Gert Bijnens, Jozef Konings, Aaron Putseys

item.title: Data Sharing in Hybrid Marketplaces With Endogenous Fee Setting
item.description: We study a hybrid marketplace where a vertically integrated platform competes with a seller, who pays the platform a transaction fee, in a horizontally differentiated downstream market. — Federico Navarra, Flavio Pino, Luca Sandrini

item.title: Dancing to multiple tunes: Establishing legitimacy with first‐time and repeat backers in crowdfunding campaigns
item.description: Research Summary Using 14,108 Kickstarter crowdfunding campaigns, we examine three strategies to gather support from first‐time versus repeat backers: narrative distinctiveness aligning with backers' expectations of novelty, endorsement from Kickstarter… — Stephanie Hepp, Alexander Vossen, Lien Denoo

item.title: Micro‐transitions and work identity: The case of academic entrepreneurs
item.description: Research Summary This paper examines how academic entrepreneurs—scientists who found research‐based startups while remaining in academia—construct and sustain their professional identities amid frequent transitions between academic and entrepreneurial roles. — Marouane Bousfiha, Henrik Berglund

item.title: Learning to innovate: How and when firms transform intellectual capital into exploratory and exploitative innovation
item.description: Research Summary Corporate entrepreneurship (CE) requires firms to pursue both exploratory and exploitative innovation, yet limited research explains how intellectual capital (IC) is translated into these distinct outcomes. — Gholamhossein (Amir) Mehralian, Arash Sadeghi, Ralf Wilden

item.title: Paid‐free differentiation in freemium: Understanding the balance between discovery and cannibalization and its implications for paid product sales
item.description: Research Summary Entrepreneurs in digital markets often introduce free versions of their paid products to boost their visibility. This freemium strategy involves a trade‐off between discovery and cannibalization. — Joey van Angeren, Ksenia Podoynitsyna, Fred Langerak

item.title: From dual-use to omni-use: How firms' strategic responses reproduce institutional lock-in in European technology governance
item.description: Technologies with both civilian and military applications are increasingly boundaryless, yet European technology governance still classifies them through the category of dual-use. — Jonas Singer, Elisabeth F. Mueller, Rafaela Kraus

item.title: Human Capital as a Driver of Automation: Theory and Evidence From China's College Expansion
item.description: This paper studies how human capital shapes both the level and direction of automation. — Jianying Chen, Qichun He, Kai Li

item.title: The coevolution of trust and behavioral uncertainty: Toward a theory of vulnerability acceptance in entrepreneurial ventures
item.description: Research Summary This conceptual study develops a process theory of vulnerability acceptance explaining how trust and behavioral uncertainty coevolve as entrepreneurial actors form, interpret, and realize opportunities. — Lars Huemer, Jan Ketil Arnulf

item.title: Academic entrepreneurs' material engagements in the creation of science‐based ventures
item.description: Research Summary This paper examines the creation of entrepreneurial opportunities under coupled technical and demand uncertainty within science‐based ventures (SBVs). — Elimar Pires Vasconcellos, Jonathan Wareham, Laia Pujol Priego

item.title: How ventures maintain stakeholder support amidst operational legitimacy threats
item.description: Research Summary We explore how ventures mitigate operational legitimacy threats—threats that originate within the venture and challenge claims relating to the venture's ability to deliver on its promised value proposition. — Alex Murray, Susan Cohen, Farhan Iqbal

item.title: Logical reframing: A theory‐based view of entrepreneurial persuasion
item.description: Research Summary Prior literature that addresses how entrepreneurs systematically deal with Knightian uncertainty has primarily focused on individual entrepreneurs but has largely neglected that, to be successful, entrepreneurs must also persuade others of their view of the future. — Timo Ehrig, Jens Schmidt

item.title: Multidimensional mechanism design and robust revenue maximization in multi-object auctions
item.description: — Hiroyuki Adachi

item.title: All-pay quality-bids in score procurement auctions
item.description: — Dan Kovenock, Jingfeng Lu

item.title: Orchestrating the Distributive Process: Baron and Ferejohn Meet Tullock
item.description: — Qiang Fu, Zenan Wu, Yuxuan Zhu

item.title: Sequential Non-Bayesian Persuasion
item.description: — Yaron Azrieli, Rachana Das

item.title: Poverty traps under endogenous discounting
item.description: — Stefano Bosi, Thai Ha-Huy

item.title: Industrialization, class conflict, and the closing window of democratic opportunity
item.description: This paper addresses two long-standing questions in the political economy of development: how the timing of industrialization affects the transition to democracy and how different social classes shape that transition. — Stephen L. Parente, Luis Felipe Sáenz, Anna Seim

item.title: Carbon emissions regulation, input-output networks, and firm dynamics: The case of a low-carbon-zone pilot in China
item.description: Input-output linkages among sectors and firms are largely overlooked when assessing regulatory policies. — Xiangyu Shi, Chang Wang

item.title: Happy Pills? The Health Consequences of the Dramatic Increase in Antidepressant Use
item.description: This paper examines the health consequences of the rapid increase in antidepressant consumption in Switzerland (2002–2014). — Giuliano Masiero, Fabrizio Mazzonna, Sandro Steinbach

item.title: Large language models and economic history: A comment on Ferrara (2026)
item.description: — Johan Fourie

item.title: Quantifying undetected severe misconduct in medical research
item.description: — Katrin Hussinger, Maikel Pellens

item.title: Understanding multi-level dynamics in rural entrepreneurial ecosystems: A conceptual framework and research agenda
item.description: Rural regions occupy vast territories and often exhibit spatial dispersion, limited institutional support, constrained resources, and scarce market opportunities. Yet entrepreneurial activity develops under these conditions. — Ana Joana Candeias Fernandes, João J. Ferreira, Luís Farinha

item.title: Monopoly Versus Dual‐Channel Distribution With Multiple Retailers
item.description: This paper examines how downstream competition shapes a manufacturer's decision to adopt a dual‐channel structure—supplying independent retailers via secret two‐part tariff contracts while also operating a direct channel. — Cong Pan

item.title: Opening Hours and Consumer Behavior: Evidence From GPS Data and Deregulation
item.description: In 2019, North Dakota repealed its Sunday closing law, which had required most non‐grocery stores to close between midnight and noon. Using this policy change and consumer GPS data, we study the impact of opening hours on shopping behavior and welfare. — Javier D. Donna, Marit Hinnosaar, Toomas Hinnosaar, André Trindade

item.title: Life‐Cycle Wage Growth and Firm Productivity in Developed and Developing Economies
item.description: Life‐cycle wage growth varies substantially across countries. We study the firm productivity distribution's role in a random‐search model with learning and labor‐market frictions, estimated for Brazil, Colombia, and the United States. — Kerstin Holzheu, Juan Munoz‐Morales

item.title: Information Aggregation With Delegation of Votes
item.description: Liquid democracy (LD) combines elements of direct and representative democracy: voters can either vote directly or delegate their votes to others. — Amrita Dhillon, Grammateia Kotsialou, Dilip Ravindran, Dimitrios Xefteris

item.title: Growing Pains: Inefficient Resource Allocation in Emerging Economies
item.description: This paper investigates how economic catch‐up shapes resource allocation in emerging economies. I develop a model that features firm‐specific technology adoption and costly adjustment of production factors. — Li Anpeng

item.title: Place‐Based Land Policy and Spatial Misallocation: Theory and Evidence From China
item.description: We investigate a land policy in China that allocated more urban land quotas to underdeveloped regions to reduce regional gaps. Empirically, the policy decreased productivity in eastern areas relative to the inland. — Min Fang, Libin Han, Zibin Huang, Ming Lu, Li Zhang

item.title: From critique to catalyst: How academic entrepreneurs transform negative feedback into pivots and performance
item.description: Research Summary This study examines how academic entrepreneurs refine business ideas in response to external critique and how these responses relate to performance. — D. Carrington Motley, Michael Leatherbee, Riitta Katila

item.title: The signal of institutional governance in early‐stage financing for university spinoffs
item.description: Research Summary University spinoffs (USOs) translate scientific advancement to economic gains, but the role of the university's governance as a public or private institution is infrequently explored. — Andrea Belz, Alexandra Graddy‐Reed, Fernando Zapatero

item.title: Accounting for the Evolution of China's Production and Trade Patterns
item.description: We study the evolution of China's production and trade patterns during its integration into the global economy. Using firm‐level microdata, we document how production and exports shifted across industries and within industries across firms. — Hanwei Huang, Jiandong Ju, Vivian Z. Yue

item.title: Asset Market Participation, Redistribution, and Asset Pricing
item.description: We study how redistribution between asset holders and non‐asset holders links macroeconomic fluctuations to expected stock returns. Aggregate and relative consumption growth forecast excess returns with opposite signs and at different horizons. — Francesco Saverio Gaudio, Ivan Petrella, Emiliano Santoro

item.title: Multi‐Agent Contracting With Network Externalities
item.description: ABSTRACTThis paper analyzes how the structure of externalities‐encompassing both pure spillovers and interactive components‐reshapes the classic trade‐off between incentives and risk in multi‐agent contracts. — Yang Sun, Wei Zhao

item.title: The Dynamics of the Racial Wealth Gap
item.description: We study the dynamics of the racial wealth gap (the wealth of Black households relative to white ones) using a dynamic equilibrium model of overlapping generations. We match the model to the cross‐sectional distributions of wealth and earnings by race. — Dionissi Aliprantis, Daniel R. Carroll, Eric R. Young

item.title: The Decentralization of Liquor Policies in Texas During the Post‐Prohibition Era
item.description: We examine the decentralization of liquor policies in Texas during the Post‐Prohibition era using newly collected historical legislative roll call data. — Andrew Arnold, Holger Sieg

item.title: Value Created, Value Leaked: Shareholder Activism and Employee-Initiated Data Leaks
item.description: Financially motivated shareholder activism is a well-established mechanism for enhancing shareholder value, improving governance, and driving operational efficiency. — Mark DesJardine, Jue Wang

item.title: Agricultural Trade and Industrial Development
item.description: Is agricultural productivity conducive to economic development? We develop a two‐country open‐economy Schumpeterian growth model with endogenous takeoff. — Angus C. Chu, Yuichi Furukawa, Pietro F. Peretto, Rongxin Xu

item.title: Rational Expectations Fools' Bubbles
item.description: We develop a rational, Walrasian model of speculative bubbles inspired by the Kindleberger–Minsky view, which describes bubbles as wave‐like market processes. — Luis Araujo, Antonio Doblas‐Madrid

item.title: The Interaction Between Credit and Labor Market Frictions
